training.checkpoint_note: RSL-RL saves at iteration % 100 == 0 on the absolute index plus the final checkpoint; the nominal 24750..25150 list in the training plan mispredicted this alignment and was amended before any probe episode

hypothesis: Command-relative tracking kernels sigma(c)=clip(0.35*|c|, 0.10, 0.50) for lin xy and yaw with a 500-update budget at lr cap 1e-5 and retention 45% should move the magnitude-0.3 undershoot past the declared advance rule
hypothesis_verdict: partially falsified: lateral moved, yaw did not reach the rule, advance rule failed for all six children

findings.lateral: dose-dependent improvement: lateral_small 0.773 -> 0.833/0.869 (24700/25150); rough_06 +0.3 reaches 0.848 with 1/5 fails at 25100; the kernel mechanism works for lateral
findings.yaw: plateaus at 0.71-0.74 mean (gain +0.02..+0.04) with left/right asymmetry (flat -0.3 0.64-0.71 vs +0.3 0.66-0.76); not reachable from the 25k-update prior via 500 more updates
findings.stairs: retention 45% protected stairs: traverse_0.5/0.7 crossed 5/5 for every child (focus-kernel children had lost these); wheel torque saturation on stairs_up dropped 12.8% -> 10.4-12.2%
findings.actuators: children are smoother than the parent on rough: wheel torque saturation 3.0% -> 1.6-2.6%, wheel rolling residual (slip) 5.13 -> 2.36-2.89 m/s peak
findings.longitudinal: 1-s moving-window violations on +-1.0 remain 5/5 cells for every policy including the parent; late checkpoints (25100/25150) lose longitudinal episode passes (0/10) via the same windows

interpretation: Continuation from a policy trained 20k updates under the wide kernel cannot reach ratio >= 0.8 on 0.3 commands: the undershoot equilibrium is baked into the actor prior even when the reward no longer tolerates it. The relative kernel is validated as a mechanism (lateral moves, actuators smooth, stairs protected with higher retention), which supports the contingency: a full retrain from upstream_19999 with the relative kernel from the first update
